W3119132889.title: Convolutional neural network for smoke and fire semantic segmentation
W3119132889.contest_reason: S1: motivated by wildfires, but the stated deployment is a camera embedded in a vehicle; the abstract never establishes wildland imagery.

W3204651913.title: Forest Fire Detection System using ZigBee
W3204651913.contest_reason: Evidence insufficiency: a forest fire detection system is described and no evaluation of it is reported anywhere in the abstract.

W4396670524.title: An Analysis of Internet-of-Things-Based Fire Detection and Alert Systems
W4396670524.contest_type: document type unresolvable from the abstract
W4396670524.contest_reason: S3: titled 'An Analysis of' and reads like a survey, but describes a built device. Only the full text could settle it, and we do not have it.

W3176110204.title: Wildfire Detection From Multisensor Satellite Imagery Using Deep Semantic Segmentation
W3176110204.contest_reason: S2: titled 'Wildfire Detection', but the workflow is repeatedly described as detection of fire-AFFECTED AREAS, with burned-area framing throughout.

W3180371431.title: Ground-Based Corroboration of GOES-17 Fire Detection Capabilities During Ignition of the Kincade Fire
W3180371431.contest_type: measures detection but proposes no method
W3180371431.contest_reason: S2: wildland fire, and detection latency is the measured quantity, but the paper corroborates an existing detector rather than contributing one.

W4312250248.title: Wildland Fire Detection and Monitoring Using a Drone-Collected RGB/IR Image Dataset
W4312250248.contest_reason: S3: a dataset paper that also reports detection baselines. If a benchmark release counts as a primary method study, IN; if not, OUT.

W4399361386.title: An open flame and smoke detection dataset for deep learning in remote sensing based fire detection
W4399361386.contest_reason: S3: same ambiguity as FLAME2, coded the same way for consistency.

W4394697163.title: YOLOv5 vs. YOLOv8: Performance Benchmarking in Wildfire and Smoke Detection Scenarios
W4394697163.contest_reason: S1: titled and framed as wildfire detection, evaluated on the Foggia dataset, which is general fire video rather than wildland-specific.

W7198168751.title: Development of a model for segmentation of forest fires on satellite images using neural network technologies
W7198168751.contest_reason: The abstract field holds a bibliographic citation string, not an abstract. The decision rests on the title alone, which is the very failure mode this paper documents in others.
